runs.text: The Company was incorporated on March 22, 2021 as Investcorp Asia Acquisition Corp I, a Cayman Islands exempted company. The Company changed its name to Investcorp Europe Acquisition Corp I on October 7, 2021 and to Invest Acquisition Corporation on December 17, 2024. The Company was formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses (a “business combination”). The Company is an emerging growth company and a “shell company” as defined under the Exchange Act, having conducted no operations and generated no revenue, with nominal assets consisting almost entirely of cash. The Company’s executive offices are located at 9th Floor, 60 Nexus Way, Camana Bay, P.O. Box 190, George Town, Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands KY1-1104, and its telephone number is +1 (345) 949-4900.

On December 17, 2021, the Company consummated its IPO of 34,500,000 units (including 4,500,000 units from the full exercise of the underwriters’ overallotment option) at $10.00 per unit, generating gross proceeds of $345.0 million and incurring offering costs of approximately $20.1 million, including $12.075 million of deferred underwriting commissions. Simultaneously, the Company completed a private placement of 16,700,000 warrants to its sponsor at $1.00 per warrant, generating gross proceeds of $16.7 million. Upon closing, $351.9 million ($10.20 per unit) was placed in a trust account with Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company acting as trustee.

On March 7, 2023, the Company entered into a non-interest bearing convertible unsecured loan (the “March 2023 Loan”) with a sponsor affiliate for up to $2,000,000 to fund working capital and Extension Contributions. Amounts used for working capital were not deposited into the trust account. In the event the Company did not consummate a business combination by June 17, 2024, the March 2023 Loan would be repaid only from funds outside the trust account or forfeited. The loan is convertible into private placement warrants of the post-business combination entity at $1.00 per warrant, on terms identical to the existing private placement warrants.

On March 14, 2023, the Company held an extraordinary general meeting at which shareholders approved proposals to extend the deadline to complete an initial business combination from March 17, 2023 to December 17, 2023 and to remove the net tangible asset redemption limitation. In connection with the meeting, 15,494,333 of the 34,500,000 public shares were redeemed at approximately $10.43 per share, leaving 19,005,667 public shares outstanding and approximately $198.2 million in the trust account. In connection with the extension, the Sponsor agreed to contribute to the trust account the lesser of $350,000 or $0.03 per non-redeemed public share for each monthly extension period through the earlier of the completion of a business combination or the end of the extension period, funded through monthly advances on the March 2023 Loan.

On April 25, 2023, the Company entered into a Business Combination Agreement (as subsequently amended, the “Business Combination Agreement”) with Zacco Holdings (formerly OpSec Holdings), a Cayman Islands exempted company (“Pubco”), certain merger subsidiaries of Pubco, Orca Holdings Limited (“Orca”) and its subsidiaries, and the shareholders of Orca, Investcorp Technology Secondary Fund 2018, L.P. (“ITSF”) and Mill Reef Capital Fund ScS (collectively, the “Orca Shareholders”). Pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement, and subject to certain terms and conditions, the Orca Shareholders would have contributed all outstanding ordinary shares of Orca to Pubco in exchange for 23,577,550 Pubco Ordinary Shares, $10,000,000 in cash, and the right to receive up to an additional 1,277,550 Pubco Ordinary Shares upon the occurrence of certain triggering events, following which the Company would have merged with and into a subsidiary of Pubco, with Class A ordinary shares and warrants of the Company being exchanged for corresponding Pubco securities. In connection with the Business Combination Agreement, the Company and certain related parties entered into ancillary agreements, including a Backstop Agreement pursuant to which the Sponsor committed to purchase up to $50,000,000 in Pubco equity securities, a Sponsor Support Agreement providing for, among other things, the cancellation of 2,555,100 Class B ordinary shares and the transfer of 2,050,000 warrants to the Orca Shareholders, and lock-up and registration rights agreements.

The Business Combination Agreement was subsequently amended on five occasions. On December 14, 2023, the First Amendment provided certain Orca option holders the right to elect to cash out up to 10% of their options, cancelled certain executive options, and established a seven-member post-closing Pubco board. On March 10, 2024, the Second Amendment was entered into concurrently with a stock purchase agreement for the divestiture of the OpSec business conducted through Orca Bidco and its subsidiaries (the “Divestiture”), with the Zacco business being retained by Orca Midco. The Divestiture was consummated on May 7, 2024, with net proceeds deposited into a third-party escrow account. The Second Amendment also provided for the conversion of Class B ordinary shares into Class A ordinary shares (effected January 2, 2024), added representations, warranties and covenants regarding the Zacco business, required delivery of audited Zacco financial statements, established a fairness opinion process, and added termination rights in favor of the Company with associated termination payments ranging from $25,000,000 to $30,000,000 depending on the timing and nature of the termination event. On May 3, 2024, the Third Amendment provided for the payment of specified transaction expenses from the escrow account, the release of $7,800,000 to the Company for settlement of expenses, established a two-tranche advance structure for Orca Midco, and provided that termination amounts would be reduced by amounts previously advanced to the Company plus notional interest at 8% per annum. On August 4, 2024, the Fourth Amendment provided for the release of an additional $1,195,643 to the Company for settlement of expenses and extended the Company’s termination right through August 30, 2024. On August 30, 2024, the Fifth Amendment revised the post-closing Pubco board composition to six members, shortened the post-closing dividend timeline to five business days, required reasonable best efforts to arrange third-party financing to facilitate such dividend, and extended the Company’s termination right through September 30, 2024.

In April 2023, the Company entered into engagement letters with each of its underwriters to act as capital markets advisor and placement agent in connection with the Business Combination. On June 9, 2023, the Company terminated its engagement letters with Credit Suisse pursuant to provisions that permitted termination if certain key team members ceased to remain actively involved, with no fees due thereunder. In connection with the termination, Credit Suisse waived its contractual right to the deferred underwriting fee from the Company’s IPO. The Company’s indemnification and contribution obligations to Credit Suisse under the underwriting agreement dated December 14, 2021 and the engagement letters survived such termination.

Additionally, during 2023, the Company entered into non-interest bearing unsecured loans with an affiliate of the Sponsor in the aggregate principal amount of up to $3,450,000 (the “Loans”) to provide additional non-interest bearing working capital and fund monthly trust account contributions. The Loans were due and payable upon the earlier of consummation of a business combination or the effective date of the Company’s winding up, and were repayable only from funds held outside the trust account if no business combination was consummated by the extended deadline.

On December 5, 2023, the Company held an extraordinary general meeting at which shareholders approved a proposal to extend the deadline to complete an initial business combination from December 17, 2023 to June 17, 2024. In connection with the extension, 7,460,372 of the 19,005,667 outstanding public shares were redeemed at approximately $11.00 per share, leaving 11,545,295 public shares outstanding and approximately $127.0 million in the trust account. The Sponsor agreed to contribute monthly to the trust account the lesser of $150,000 or $0.02 per non-redeemed public share for each monthly period during the extension until the earlier of the completion of an initial business combination or the end of the extension period.

On December 22, 2023 (effected January 2, 2024), the initial shareholders voluntarily converted 8,624,999 Class B ordinary shares into Class A ordinary shares on a one-for-one basis. All terms and conditions applicable to the Class B ordinary shares, including voting agreements, transfer restrictions, and waiver of rights to the trust account, continued to apply to the converted shares. Following the conversion, there were 20,170,294 Class A ordinary shares outstanding (11,545,295 held by public shareholders and 8,624,999 held by the initial shareholders) and one Class B ordinary share outstanding held by the Sponsor. The conversion had no effect on aggregate voting power or the votes required to approve proposals in connection with the Business Combination.

On May 21, 2024 shareholders approved an extension of the Business Combination deadline from June 17, 2024, to December 17, 2024. In connection with this vote, 2,159,610 Class A shares were redeemed for approximately $24.4 million.
The Company filed an application to trade its Class A ordinary shares, units, and warrants on the OTCQB Market under the symbols “IVCBF,” “IVCUF,” and “IVCWF,” respectively.
Termination of the Business Combination Agreement

On September 24, 2024, the Special Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company determined, in good faith after consultation with its outside counsel and other advisors, that the consummation of the Transactions following the Divestiture Closing was not advisable, fair to, or in the best interests of the Company and the Company’s shareholders (other than the Sponsor) in accordance with the Companies Act (as revised) of the Cayman Islands. Accordingly, the Company terminated the Business Combination Agreement effective as of September 24, 2024 pursuant to Section 12.1(h) thereof. Under the terms of the Business Combination Agreement, the Company was entitled to a termination amount (“Termination Payment”) of $30.0 million. The $30.0 million termination amount was satisfied through a combination of transactions, including (i) the payment of the Orca Midco promissory note totaling approximately $9.3 million, consisting of approximately $7.8 million of specified transaction expenses, approximately $1.2 million of transaction expenses, and approximately $0.3 million of accrued interest; (ii) approximately $10.3 million of proceeds released from the divestiture escrow account on September 26, 2024; and (iii) a novation and payment arrangement totaling approximately $10.4 million, comprised of the assignment of approximately $6.9 million of outstanding Investcorp Funding loans to Orca Midco Limited and a cash payment of approximately $3.5 million, together satisfying the remaining outstanding portion of the termination amount.
Pro Rata Distribution of the Termination Payment

On October 22, 2024, the Company’s Board of Directors declared a distribution of the net amount of the Termination Payment after satisfaction of the Company’s liabilities pro rata to all holders of Class A ordinary shares, equal to $0.60 per Class A ordinary share, paid on November 12, 2024 to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 4, 2024. The pro rata distribution of the net amount of the Termination Payment had no impact on the rights of holders of the Class A ordinary shares, including with regard to liquidation rights or redemption of the trust account.

On December 16, 2024, the Company’s original sponsor, Europe Acquisition Holdings Limited, and its directors (the “Sellers”) entered into a Purchase Agreement with Samara Special Opportunities (the “Acquirer”), a Cayman Islands exempted company, pursuant to which the Acquirer purchased 6,037,499 Class A ordinary shares, one Class B ordinary share, and 11,690,000 private placement warrants for an aggregate purchase price of $1.00. In connection with the closing of the Purchase Agreement on December 23, 2024, Baroness Ruby McGregor-Smith (CEO), Craig Sinfield-Hain (CFO and Chairman), and Alptekin Diler (CIO) resigned from their respective positions, and Vikas Mittal, the sole director of the Acquirer and Managing Member of Meteora Capital, LLC, was appointed as CEO, CFO, and sole director of the Company. Following redemptions, Mr. Mittal may be deemed to beneficially own approximately 91.2% of the Company’s issued and outstanding ordinary shares. As of December 31, 2024, there were no amounts outstanding under any working capital loans from the sponsor.

On December 17, 2024, shareholders approved an extension of the deadline to consummate a business combination to December 17, 2025. In connection with the meeting, holders of 7,360,165 Class A ordinary shares exercised redemption rights. Also on December 17, 2024, the Company received notice from the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Department that its securities would be delisted for failure to complete an initial business combination within 36 months of its IPO. Trading on Nasdaq was suspended at the opening of business on December 24, 2024. The Company subsequently filed an application to trade its Class A ordinary shares, units, and warrants on the OTCQB Market under the symbols “IVCBF,” “IVCUF,” and “IVCWF,” respectively.

On December 12, 2025, shareholders approved the name change to Invest Acquisition Corporation and approved an extension of the deadline to consummate a business combination to December 17, 2027. In connection with the meeting, holders of 18,226 Class A ordinary shares exercised redemption rights.

On September 24, 2026, shareholders approved an extension of the deadline to consummate a business combination to December 17, 2029. In connection with the meeting, holders of 1,801,349 Class A ordinary shares exercised redemption rights.

The Company seeks to identify and consummate a business combination with one or more businesses that the Company’s management believes will create value for shareholders. In evaluating prospective targets, management considers, among other factors, the target’s growth potential, competitive position, management quality, cash flow characteristics, and readiness to operate as a public company. These criteria are not exhaustive, and management may determine to pursue a business combination with a target that does not meet all of the foregoing criteria. In the event the Company enters into a business combination with a target that does not meet the criteria described herein, such determination will be disclosed in the proxy solicitation or tender offer materials filed with the SEC in connection with the business combination.

The Company has until December 17, 2029 to consummate an initial business combination. In evaluating prospective target businesses, management conducts due diligence that may include meetings with incumbent management and employees, document reviews, customer and supplier interviews, facility inspections, and review of financial and other information. The Company’s due diligence processes and evaluation criteria are not intended to be exhaustive, and management may consider additional factors it deems relevant.

The Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association require that any initial business combination have an aggregate fair market value of at least 80% of the net assets held in the trust account (excluding deferred underwriting commissions) at the time of signing a definitive agreement. The board of directors will determine the fair market value of any proposed business combination. If the board is unable to independently make such determination, the Company will obtain an opinion from an independent investment banking or valuation firm. Any initial business combination must be approved by a majority of the Company’s shareholders entitled to vote and by the board of directors in accordance with Cayman Islands law and the Company’s governing documents.

The Company is not listed on a national securities exchange and is not subject to exchange-mandated requirements, including independent director approval of business combinations or pre-approval requirements for transactions involving targets whose auditors are not subject to PCAOB inspection. If the Company proposes a business combination with such a target, it will disclose this limitation and associated risks in materials provided to shareholders.

The Company anticipates structuring its initial business combination so that the post-transaction company owns or acquires 100% of the equity interests or assets of the target business. However, the Company may structure a business combination to acquire less than 100% of such interests, provided the post-transaction company owns at least 50% of the outstanding voting securities of the target or otherwise acquires a controlling interest sufficient to avoid registration under the Investment Company Act. The Company’s shareholders prior to the business combination may collectively own a minority interest in the post-transaction company depending on the valuations ascribed to the target and the Company. If less than 100% of a target is acquired, the portion acquired will be used for purposes of the 80% net assets test. If the business combination involves multiple targets, the test will be applied on an aggregate basis.

The time and costs required to identify, evaluate, and complete an initial business combination are not currently ascertainable. If the Company does not complete a particular business combination, costs incurred will reduce funds available for other combinations.

The Company’s officers and directors may have interests in other business ventures and are not required to commit any specified amount of time to the Company’s affairs, which may create conflicts of interest in allocating time and identifying business combination opportunities.

The Company is not prohibited from pursuing an initial business combination with a company that is affiliated with its sponsor, officers, or directors, or completing a business combination through a joint venture or other form of shared ownership with the sponsor, officers, or directors. In the event the Company seeks to complete an initial business combination with a company affiliated with its sponsor, officers, or directors, the Company will obtain an opinion from an independent investment banking firm that is a member of FINRA that such business combination is fair to the Company from a financial point of view.

Unless the Company completes an initial business combination with an affiliated entity, or its sole director cannot independently determine the fair market value of the target business, the Company is not required to obtain a fairness opinion from an independent investment banking firm, valuation firm, or independent accounting firm. If no opinion is obtained, shareholders will be relying on the business judgment of the Company’s sole director, who will have significant discretion in choosing the valuation standard used to establish fair market value. Such standards will be disclosed in the tender offer documents or proxy solicitation materials filed in connection with the initial business combination.

The Company’s sole officer and director owns founder shares and private placement warrants, directly or indirectly, and accordingly may have a conflict of interest in determining whether a particular target business is appropriate for an initial business combination. The founder shares would be worthless if the Company did not complete an initial business combination, and were acquired at a nominal cost relative to the $10.00 per unit IPO price, which could result in a substantial profit even if public investors experienced losses. The sole officer and director has fiduciary and contractual obligations to other entities, including Investcorp and its affiliates, pursuant to which he may be required to present acquisition opportunities to such entities before presenting them to the Company. The Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association provide that, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the sole officer and director has no duty to refrain from engaging in the same or similar business activities as the Company, and the Company renounced any interest in corporate opportunities that may arise. The sole officer and director is not required to commit any specified amount of time to the Company’s affairs and may have conflicts in allocating time among various business activities.

The Company has filed a Registration Statement on Form 8-A with the SEC to voluntarily register its securities under Section 12 of the Exchange Act and is subject to the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder. The Company has no current intention of filing a Form 15 to suspend its reporting obligations prior to or following consummation of an initial business combination.
Emerging Growth Company and Smaller Reporting Company Status

The Company is an “emerging growth company” as defined in the JOBS Act. The Company will remain an emerging growth company until the earlier of (1) the last day of the fiscal year (a) following the fifth anniversary of the completion of the IPO, (b) in which total annual gross revenue is at least $1.235 billion, or (c) in which the Company is deemed a large accelerated filer, and (2) the date on which the Company has issued more than $1.0 billion in non-convertible debt during the prior three-year period.

The Company is also a “smaller reporting company” as defined in Item 10(f)(1) of Regulation S-K and will remain so for each fiscal year in which (1) the market value of ordinary shares held by non-affiliates is less than $250 million as of the end of the second fiscal quarter, or (2) annual revenues are less than $100 million and such market value is less than $700 million.

The Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association require that any initial business combination have an aggregate fair market value of at least 80% of the net assets held in the trust account (excluding deferred underwriting commissions) at the time of signing a definitive agreement. The Company’s sole director will determine fair market value; if unable to do so independently, the Company will obtain an opinion from an independent investment banking or valuation firm.

The Company intends to effectuate its initial business combination using cash from trust, shares issued to target owners, debt, or a combination thereof. The Company may seek additional financing through private offerings of debt or equity securities in connection with a business combination and would expect to complete such financing simultaneously with closing. There is no limitation on the Company’s ability to raise funds through equity, equity-linked securities, or debt in connection with a business combination. As of the date of this report, the Company is not party to any arrangement with any third party with respect to raising additional funds, and no sponsor, officer, director, or shareholder is required to provide financing.

If not all funds released from the trust account are used for consideration or redemptions, the Company may use the balance for general corporate purposes, including operations, debt service, acquisitions, or working capital.

The Company may conduct redemptions without a shareholder vote pursuant to the SEC’s tender offer rules, subject to the provisions of its governing documents. The Company will seek shareholder approval if required by the Companies Act (as revised) of the Cayman Islands, its governing documents, applicable SEC rules, or if it determines shareholder approval is appropriate for business or other reasons.

As an OTC-quoted company, the Company is not subject to national securities exchange listing standards. Exchange-mandated shareholder approval requirements, including those applicable to transactions involving the issuance of 20% or more of outstanding shares, officer/director conflicts, or changes of control, do not apply. The Company’s obligations to obtain shareholder approval are governed solely by Cayman Islands law and its governing documents. Shareholders do not have the protections that exchange listing standards would otherwise provide.

If the Company seeks shareholder approval of a business combination and does not conduct redemptions pursuant to tender offer rules, the sponsor, directors, officers, advisors, or their affiliates may purchase shares or public warrants in privately negotiated transactions or in the open market prior to or following completion of a business combination, subject to compliance with applicable law and OTC rules. There is no limit on the number of securities that may be purchased, though no current commitments, plans, or intentions to engage in such transactions exist. No trust account funds will be used for such purchases, and no purchases will be made while in possession of material non-public information or in violation of Regulation M.

Such purchases could serve to satisfy minimum net worth or cash closing conditions in a business combination agreement, reduce the number of outstanding public warrants, or facilitate a business combination that might not otherwise be completed. Such purchases may reduce the public float and number of beneficial holders, which may make it difficult to maintain quotation or trading of the Company’s securities.

To the extent the sponsor, officers, directors, or their affiliates enter into private purchases, they would contact only shareholders who have expressed an election to redeem or vote against the business combination, provided such shares have not already been voted. No purchases will be made in violation of Section 9(a)(2) or Rule 10b-5 of the Exchange Act, and all purchases will be reported pursuant to Sections 13 and 16 of the Exchange Act to the extent applicable.

As of the date of this report, no agreements for private purchases of public shares have been entered into. In connection with any such purchases: (i) the sponsor or its affiliates will purchase public shares at a price no higher than the redemption price; (ii) such purchased shares will not be voted in favor of the business combination; and (iii) the sponsor and its affiliates have waived redemption rights on such shares. Prior to any extraordinary general meeting to approve a business combination, the Company will disclose in a Form 8-K the amount and price of shares purchased outside the redemption offer, the purpose and impact of such purchases on the likelihood of approval, the identities or nature of selling shareholders, and the number of shares for which redemption requests have been received.

blocks.text: Redemption Rights for Public Shareholders upon Completion of Our Initial Business Combination

runs.text: The Company’s public shareholders may redeem all or a portion of their Class A ordinary shares upon completion of an initial business combination at a per-share price, payable in cash, equal to the aggregate amount then on deposit in the trust account, calculated as of two business days prior to consummation, including interest earned and not previously released for taxes, divided by the number of then-outstanding public shares. As of September 23, 2026, approximately $24.7 million was held in the trust account, or approximately $12.31 per share. The per-share redemption amount will not be reduced by deferred underwriting commissions. The Company’s sponsor, officers, and directors have agreed to waive their redemption rights with respect to their founder shares and any public shares held in connection with the completion of an initial business combination.

A proposed initial business combination may require minimum cash amounts for consideration payable to the target, working capital, or other conditions. If the aggregate amount required to fund redemptions plus any cash conditions of the proposed business combination exceeds available cash, the Company will not complete the business combination or redeem any shares, and all shares submitted for redemption will be returned to holders. The Company may raise additional funds through equity-linked securities or debt to satisfy such requirements.
Redemption of Public Shares in Connection with a Business Combination

The Company’s public shareholders may redeem all or a portion of their Class A ordinary shares upon completion of an initial business combination either (i) in connection with a general meeting called to approve the business combination or (ii) without a shareholder vote by means of a tender offer. The decision whether to seek shareholder approval or conduct a tender offer will be made by the Company in its sole discretion based on factors including timing and whether the terms of the transaction require shareholder approval under applicable law or the Company’s governing documents.

The requirement to provide public shareholders with the opportunity to redeem by one of these methods is contained in the Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association. Such provisions may be amended by special resolution (the affirmative vote of shareholders holding not less than two-thirds of the shares voted) or unanimous written resolution, provided the Company offers redemption in connection with such amendment.
If Shareholder Approval Is Sought

If the Company seeks shareholder approval, it will conduct redemptions in conjunction with a proxy solicitation pursuant to Regulation 14A of the Exchange Act and file proxy materials with the SEC. The Company will complete the business combination only upon obtaining an ordinary resolution under Cayman Islands law (the affirmative vote of a majority of shares voted at a quorate meeting or unanimous written resolution). A quorum requires holders of a majority of issued and outstanding shares entitled to vote to be represented in person or by proxy. The Company’s sponsor, officers, and directors have agreed to vote their founder shares, private placement shares, and any public shares purchased during or after the IPO in favor of the initial business combination. If the business combination is structured as a statutory merger or consolidation under Cayman Islands law, approval will require a special resolution (two-thirds of shares voted). Each public shareholder may elect to redeem regardless of whether they vote for or against the proposed transaction or were a shareholder on the record date.
If Shareholder Approval Is Not Sought

If a shareholder vote is not required, the Company will conduct redemptions pursuant to Rule 13e-4 and Regulation 14E of the Exchange Act and file tender offer documents containing substantially the same information as would be required under Regulation 14A. The tender offer will remain open for at least 20 business days and will be conditioned on public shareholders not tendering more than the number of shares the Company is permitted to redeem. If excess shares are tendered, the Company will withdraw the tender offer and not complete the business combination. Upon public announcement of a business combination conducted pursuant to tender offer rules, any Rule 10b5-1 plan to purchase Class A ordinary shares will be terminated to comply with Rule 14e-5.

Public shareholders seeking to exercise redemption rights must deliver their share certificates to the Company’s transfer agent or deliver shares electronically using the DTC’s DWAC system prior to the date specified in the proxy materials or tender offer documents. If redemptions are conducted in connection with a shareholder vote, holders must also submit a written redemption request to the transfer agent two business days prior to the scheduled vote identifying the beneficial owner. If a proposed business combination is not approved, certificates or shares will be promptly returned.

blocks.text: Redemption of Public Shares and Liquidation If No Initial Business Combination

runs.text: The Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association provide that the Company has until December 17, 2029 (the “Extension Period”) to complete an initial business combination. If the Company does not complete a business combination within the Extension Period, it will: (i) cease all operations except for winding up; (ii) as promptly as reasonably possible but not more than ten business days thereafter, redeem the public shares at a per-share price, payable in cash, equal to the aggregate amount then on deposit in the trust account, including interest earned (less taxes payable and up to $100,000 of interest for dissolution expenses), divided by the number of then-outstanding public shares, which will extinguish public shareholders’ rights as shareholders; and (iii) liquidate and dissolve, subject to obligations under Cayman Islands law to provide for claims of creditors. Warrants will expire worthless if the Company fails to complete a business combination within the Extension Period.

As of September 23, 2026, the per-share redemption amount was approximately $12.31 based on approximately $24.7 million held in the trust account. The actual per-share amount received by shareholders may be less than this amount due to creditor claims or other factors described below.

The Company’s sponsor, officers, and directors have waived their rights to liquidating distributions from the trust account with respect to founder shares if the Company fails to complete a business combination within the Extension Period, though they are entitled to liquidating distributions on any public shares they hold. They have also agreed not to propose amendments to the governing documents that would modify the substance or timing of the Company’s redemption obligations or other material shareholder protections unless public shareholders are offered redemption in connection with such amendment.

blocks.text: Trust Account Protections and Creditor Claims

runs.text: The Company seeks to have all vendors, service providers, and prospective target businesses execute agreements waiving claims to trust account funds. However, there is no guarantee such waivers will be obtained or enforced. CBIZ CPAs P.C., the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm, has not executed such a waiver.

The Company’s sponsor has agreed to indemnify the trust account if third-party claims reduce trust funds below the lesser of (i) $10.20 per public share or (ii) the actual per-share amount held in trust as of the date of liquidation, less taxes payable. This indemnity does not apply to claims by parties that executed trust waivers or to claims under the Company’s indemnity of IPO underwriters. The Company has not verified whether the sponsor has sufficient funds to satisfy these obligations, and the sponsor’s assets are believed to consist primarily of securities of the Company. In the event the sponsor is unable to satisfy its indemnification obligations, the Company’s sole director would determine whether to take legal action to enforce such obligations. Accordingly, if creditor claims deplete the trust account, the per-share redemption amount could be less than $10.20.

Costs associated with dissolution are expected to be funded from proceeds held outside the trust account. If such funds are insufficient, the Company may use up to $100,000 of accrued trust account interest to cover dissolution expenses.

If a bankruptcy or insolvency petition is filed by or against the Company, trust account proceeds could be included in the bankruptcy estate and subject to third-party claims with priority over shareholders. Distributions received by shareholders could be challenged as preferential transfers or fraudulent conveyances under applicable law.

Public shareholders are entitled to receive funds from the trust account only upon: (i) redemption of public shares if the Company does not complete a business combination within the Extension Period; (ii) redemption in connection with a shareholder vote to amend governing documents relating to redemption obligations or other material shareholder protections; or (iii) redemption upon completion of an initial business combination. Voting on a business combination alone does not trigger redemption; shareholders must separately exercise their redemption rights.

blocks.text: Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association

runs.text: The business combination provisions of the Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association require approval by special resolution to amend. Under Cayman Islands law, a special resolution requires the affirmative vote of shareholders holding not less than two-thirds of the shares voted at a quorate general meeting, or a unanimous written resolution of all shareholders.
The governing documents provide, among other things, that:

If the Company does not complete an initial business combination within the Extension Period, it will cease all operations except for winding up, redeem 100% of public shares at a per-share price equal to the aggregate trust account balance (including interest, less taxes payable and up to $100,000 for dissolution expenses) divided by the number of outstanding public shares, and liquidate and dissolve, subject to Cayman Islands law obligations to creditors.
Prior to an initial business combination, the Company may not issue additional securities entitling holders to receive funds from the trust account or vote on the business combination.

The Company is not prohibited from pursuing a business combination with a company affiliated with its sponsor, officers, or directors. In such event, the Company will obtain a fairness opinion from an independent FINRA-member investment banking firm. Shareholders may not receive a copy of such opinion.

If a shareholder vote is not required, the Company will conduct redemptions pursuant to Rule 13e-4 and Regulation 14E and file tender offer documents with the SEC containing substantially the same information required under Regulation 14A.

Any initial business combination must have an aggregate fair market value of at least 80% of the net assets held in trust (excluding deferred underwriting commissions) at the time of signing the definitive agreement.

If shareholders approve amendments modifying the substance or timing of redemption obligations or other material shareholder protections, the Company will offer redemption to public shareholders at the then-applicable per-share trust value.
The Company will not complete an initial business combination with another blank check company or similar entity with nominal operations.
The Company views these provisions as binding obligations to shareholders and will not take action to amend or waive them without providing dissenting shareholders the opportunity to redeem.

Under Cayman Islands law, directors owe fiduciary duties to act in good faith in the best interests of the company, exercise powers for proper purposes, avoid conflicts between personal interests and duties to the company, act fairly among shareholders, and exercise independent judgment. Directors also owe a duty of care requiring them to act as a reasonably diligent person with the general knowledge, skill, and experience relevant to the role.

The Company’s sole officer and director may have fiduciary or contractual obligations to other entities, including other special purpose acquisition companies, and may present business combination opportunities to such entities rather than the Company if required by such obligations, subject to fiduciary duties under Cayman Islands law. The Company’s governing documents provide that the Company renounces its interest in any corporate opportunity offered to any director or officer unless expressly offered solely in his capacity as director or officer and the Company is able to complete the opportunity on a reasonable basis.

The Company’s sole officer and director is not required to commit full time to the Company’s affairs, which may result in conflicts in allocating time between the Company and other business activities.

The Company’s sponsor, officers, and directors have agreed to vote their founder shares and any shares purchased during or after the IPO in favor of the initial business combination. They have also waived redemption rights on founder shares and rights to liquidating distributions from the trust account if no business combination is completed within the Extension Period.

In connection with the original IPO, certain lock-up restrictions were imposed on founder shares, providing that such shares are not transferable until the earlier of (i) one year after completion of an initial business combination or (ii) the date of a subsequent liquidation, merger, or similar transaction. The private placement warrants are not transferable until 30 days following completion of an initial business combination. Because the Company’s sole officer and director owns ordinary shares and warrants directly or indirectly, he may have a conflict of interest in evaluating potential business combinations.

The Company is not prohibited from pursuing a business combination with a company affiliated with its sponsor, officer, or director. In such event, the Company will obtain a fairness opinion from an independent FINRA-member investment banking firm. No finder’s fee, consulting fee, or other compensation will be paid by the Company to the sponsor or any officer or director for services rendered in connection with the completion of an initial business combination.

The Company utilizes office space at 9th Floor, 60 Nexus Way, Camana Bay, P.O. Box 190, George Town, Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands KY1-1104 as its executive offices. The Company considers its current office space adequate for current operations.

The Company currently has one officer who serves as CEO and CFO, who is not obligated to devote any specific number of hours to the Company’s affairs but intends to devote such time as deemed necessary until completion of an initial business combination.

The Company’s securities are registered under the Exchange Act, and the Company is subject to periodic reporting obligations, including the filing of annual, quarterly, and current reports with the SEC containing financial statements audited by the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm.

In connection with any proposed business combination, the Company will provide shareholders with audited financial statements of the prospective target business prepared in accordance with, or reconciled to, GAAP or IFRS, as applicable, and which may be required to be audited in accordance with PCAOB standards. These requirements may limit the pool of potential target businesses or affect the timing of a business combination.

The Company is required to evaluate its internal control procedures as required by the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. As an emerging growth company, the Company is not required to have its internal controls audited until it becomes a large accelerated filer or an accelerated filer and no longer qualifies as an emerging growth company.

The Company is a Cayman Islands exempted company and has received a tax exemption undertaking from the Cayman Islands government, effective for 30 years from April 6, 2021, providing that no Cayman Islands law imposing tax on profits, income, gains, or appreciations will apply to the Company or its operations, and no estate duty, inheritance tax, or withholding tax will be payable on the Company’s shares, debentures, or other obligations.

blocks.text: Emerging Growth Company and Smaller Reporting Company Status

runs.text: The Company is an “emerging growth company” as defined in the JOBS Act. As such, the Company is eligible for certain exemptions from reporting requirements applicable to other public companies, including exemption from the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, reduced executive compensation disclosure obligations, and exemptions from non-binding advisory votes on executive compensation. The Company intends to take advantage of the extended transition period for adopting new or revised accounting standards available to emerging growth companies under Section 7(a)(2)(B) of the Securities Act.

The Company will remain an emerging growth company until the earlier of (1) the last day of the fiscal year (a) following the fifth anniversary of the IPO, (b) in which total annual gross revenue is at least $1.235 billion, or (c) in which the Company is deemed a large accelerated filer, and (2) the date on which the Company has issued more than $1.0 billion in non-convertible debt during the prior three-year period.

The Company is also a “smaller reporting company” as defined in Item 10(f)(1) of Regulation S-K, providing certain reduced disclosure obligations including two years of audited financial statements. The Company will remain a smaller reporting company for each fiscal year in which (1) the market value of ordinary shares held by non-affiliates is less than $250 million as of the end of the second fiscal quarter, or (2) annual revenues are less than $100 million and such market value is less than $700 million.

There is no material litigation, arbitration, or governmental proceeding currently pending against the Company or any member of its management team in their capacity as such, and neither the Company nor its management team has been subject to any such proceeding in the 12 months preceding the date of this report.
